newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Demand poor, Thai rubber seen picking up.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Demand poor, Thai rubber seen picking up.

text.p: Weak consumer demand is seen continuing to weigh on Southeast Asian prices this week although some buying is seen shoring up prices in the Thai market, regional traders said on Monday.
"Demand is still flat," a senior dealer for a Japanese rubber trading house in Singapore told Reuters. "There are just no overseas buyers who we can see going into the market."
The sentiment was echoed by dealers in Indonesia and Malaysia.
"Region-wide, demand is not very good and it's worse here, because the prices are much higher than Indonesia," a trader in the Malaysian capital of Kuala Lumpur said.
"Market sentiment remains bearish and we expect it to continue until next week as demand is still poor," a dealer based in Indonesia added.

The only light for sellers was provided by Thailand, where the market was buoyed by higher prices in Tokyo and reports the government reportedly bought 3,000 tonnes of rubber at a higher than average price of 123.50 U.S. cents a kg.

News that Mitsui Corp last Friday signed a counter trade deal to buy 540 million baht worth of rice, rubber, tapioca and other goods in exchange for selling up to 18 billion baht worth of equipment also boosted sentiment.

Thai benchmark RSS3 grade rubber for April delivery was quoted around 123 cents a kg FOB Bangkok last week from 122.00-122.50 cents a kg on the same basis the previous week. Latex was seen at 94 cents a kg on the same basis.
"I see the prices being supported at this level this week. I think the demand will pick up as there have been quite active inquiries," a rubber trader in Hat Yai said.
"The major factor was the higher Tokyo prices. Except for the rumoured government purchase, the real demand was rather light," the dealer added.
In Indonesia, traders said buyers seemed to be waiting for further price falls before going into the market.
They said offer prices were quoted at 52.00 U.S. cents a lb FOB Palembang for March/April shipment following some overnight buying last Thursday and at 52.50 cents a lb FOB Surabaya.
Offer prices were unchanged at 52.50 cents a lb FOB Medan, but in Padang levels were easier at 51.75 cents. Traders offered SIR20 at 51.25 cents FOB Pontianak and Jambi.
Some traders said they may have to sell at 50.00 cents a lb in the future if buyers continued to stay away from the market.

"This situation can be worse if the wintering period in Sumatra ends. When supply is ample but buyers are scant, traders may have to sell at the cheapest prices possible in order to survive," a trader in Indonesia said.
Dealers believe major buyers in the U.S. and Europe had also shifted their attention to Thailand due to lower prices there.
The Malaysian market, in the meantime, will probably remain directionless this week due to soft demand, traders said.
"It's not going anywhere far from here, the way I see it," a dealer with a rubber trading house in Kuala Lumpur said.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted benchmark RSS1 grade rubber at 305.50 Malaysian cents a kg and the SMR20 at 293 cents a kg, both for April buyer, at the close of trade last week.
Malaysian-based dealers expect both rubber grades to fluctuate "one cent up or down this week."

They said the MRELB has been basically "fine-tuning" prices for the past few months in tandem with the Japanese futures market and Indonesian prices -- which are always lower because of the country's lower costs.
Stocks of latex and processed rubber were ample in the Malaysian market after months of virtually no new sales, the dealers said.
Latex was trading at 237 cents a kg at the close of the Malaysian market on Friday.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
